data.content_ref: inline:The target identifies reduced sky view factor (urban geometry) as the single dominant cross-city modulator, but the dominant *single* mechanism explaining why the night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others is widely documented as differences in *released stored heat* (thermal mass/heat capacity), not sky view factor. The target's own mechanism description conflates the two ('reduced sky view factor further delays the release of stored heat'), but it explicitly names the radiation trap as dominant and relegates stored heat to a secondary role. By privileging geometry over heat storage, it under-explains why dense cities with similar building heights but very different thermal mass / anthropogenic heat inventories can show very different nocturnal UHI gaps, which is the substantive cross-city variation the problem asks about.
